Cloud computing is everywhere—and you're probably using it without even realizing it. Gmail, Netflix, Spotify, Dropbox... they all run on cloud infrastructure.

But what exactly is it? Simply put: you're renting computing power and storage from a provider instead of buying and maintaining physical servers. The global market hit $591.8B in 2023 and will exceed $1.2 trillion by 2032.

The real magic? You only pay for what you use. Providers handle maintenance, security updates, and scaling—no more idle hardware collecting dust in your data center.

There are three main service types: SaaS (use software online), PaaS (build apps on managed platforms), and IaaS (rent bare servers you configure yourself).

Curious about how cloud computing works and whether it's right for your organization? Read our beginner's guide for the full breakdown.
